blocks.content: Under Article 169 of the Constitution, Parliament can create or abolish a Legislative Council if the Legislative Assembly of the state concerned passes a resolution to that effect by a special majority.

rows: Lower House / Directly elected / Subject to dissolution
Upper House / Indirectly elected / Permanent body
Exclusive power to introduce and pass Money Bills
Cannot reject; can only delay for up to 14 days
Cannot be abolished; dissolved every 5 years
Can be abolished under Art. 169; cannot be dissolved

items: Cooperative Movement is an additional category for Governor nominations in the Legislative Council, which is not present in Presidential nominations for the Rajya Sabha.
Money Bills cannot be introduced in the Legislative Council and can be delayed by it for a maximum of only 14 days.
Unlike the Rajya Sabha, which cannot be abolished, the Legislative Council can be completely abolished by Parliament.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) is the upper house of a state legislature and functions as a permanent body not subject to dissolution.
Under Article 169, Parliament can create or abolish a Legislative Council if the State Legislative Assembly passes a resolution by a special majority.
The total strength of the Council cannot exceed one-third of the total strength of the Assembly, nor can it be less than 40 members.
1/6th of total members are nominated by the Governor from fields of literature, science, art, cooperative movement, and social service.
The Legislative Council lacks equal powers with the Legislative Assembly and can delay an ordinary bill for a maximum period of 4 months.
